The thing is: reddit is perfectly able to scale its numbers of Amazon cloud instances to demand, but their problem has always been reacting to (predictable!) rises in demand ahead of time, even with the amount of data Google Analytics can provide them. There are some notable exceptions like popular /r/IAmA threads, which are delegated to dedicated application servers.

It's just not more prevalent because their idle amount of servers is already so high, effectively each of your requests is handled by a different server. Usually you don't hit the once instance busy with rendering several huge /r/AskReddit threads twice in a row.

Hey guys,

I've noticed that v/gamedev is a little quiet at the moment (as is to be expected with a growing community) - so what kind of community have we got on here for developers? Not just coders, mind; artists, modelers, musicians, the whole crew.

Report in, let us know what you're working on. Show off some of your work. Tell us about how many projects you've scrapped in the past year (seriously, I'm currently in a huge struggle to break out of the "develop a mechanic, test mechanic, enjoy mechanic, scrap entire project" loop). Get (hopefully in the best possible sense) judged on it.

This is what I'm currently working on. I wanted to step back from all the over-complicated stuff with massive feature creep that has plagued me in my past 2 years of game dev, and focus on a small enough product to actually push out the door. I decided on looking towards a basic platformer, following your basic mario logic. This is obviously emphasised by the test bed stage being a recreation of Mario's 1-1.

This has been built with Unity3D and C#; and there's actually quite a lot of code under the hood. Ever try to make nice hitboxes and collision detection for an impossibly long dog? At one stage I had around 8 hitboxes that switched on/off depending on the player's state (i.e; when jumping up, allow for head hits; turn off head hitbox when falling down to avoid the dog balancing on blocks with only his face). Recreating everything in using the PhysX system was pretty fun; and allowed for the fancy brick-breaking.

The game is mostly being developed with one of my best friends (A dachshund enthusiast), and my little brother in mind. Which gives me a target market of.. 2. The game will likely be released on free web portals ala Kongregate within the next 2-3 months.

So - what have you guys been working on?
